These are just some notes I made for myself about the position of the Triad Chords in the key of D Major as they appear on the first three strings of the guitar. I thought maybe someone might find it useful.

The Triads in the key of D are...
D Major, E minor, F# minor, G Major, A Major, B minor, C# diminished.


Triads in key of D on first three strings (e,b,g) ascending the neck...

DM Em F#m GM AM Bm C#dim DM (M=Major, m=minor, dim=diminished)

f# g a b c# d e f# (E string)
d e f# g a b c# d (B string)
a b c# d e f# g a (G string)


Two shapes (Major and minor) used to finger them and the place of the note in the major scale...

Major Shape (fingers used: 2, 3, 1):
x (3rd of Major scale)
 x (Root of Major scale)
x (5th of Major Scale)

Minor Shape (fingers used: 1, 3, 2): 
x (Flat 3rd of Major Scale)
 x (Root of Major Scale)
 x (5th of Major Scale)

So the 3rd (or flat 3rd if minor) is always on the e string, the root is always on the b string and the 5th is always on the g string.
